newsitem.title: TANZANIA: U.N. Rwanda trial hears accused buried bodies.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Rwanda trial hears accused buried bodies.

text.p: The U.N.'s Rwanda genocide trial of a former vice-president of the extremist Interahamwe militia resumed on Monday with the court hearing how the accused helped bury bodies of people killed.

Witness "E", so called to protect his identity, told the court he saw accused Georges Rutaganda, 39, supervise disposal of bodies on April 8, 1994, two-days after the assassination of President Juvenal Habyarimana.
"Rutaganda was wearing a pair of civilian trousers with a military jacket but he did not carry any weapon. If he had a gun I did not see it," witness "E" told the court.

"A hole had to be dug. You could see that Rutaganda was concerned because he gave us the idea to go and bury the bodies far from the road so that if the international community came they wouldn't be able to see the place," said the witness in French.
The witness earlier identified Rutaganda, a former businessman, in court and described how ethnic tension rose in Rwanda between 1990 and 1994.
"People were not safe. There were some upheavals and sometimes grenades were thrown in residential areas," the witness said.
Rutaganda's trial at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) started in March but was suspended for the tribunal's plenary session.
The session, which ended last Friday, reinstated tribunal President Laity Kama of Senegal for a second two-year term and swore in two new judges.

The ICTR was modelled on the Hague-based criminal tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, which was set up by the U.N. Security Council in 1993 and was the first international body for the prosecution of war crimes since the Nuremberg and Tokyo trials after World War Two.
The Rwanda tribunal has been plagued by problems in attempting to bring to justice the leaders of the 1994 genocide in Rwanda of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
So far 21 people have been indicted by the Rwanda tribunal, which has a total of 12 suspects in detention in Arusha, northern Tanzania.
